title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of week lost. Historical closure effect not available, but store closures reduce demand proportionally. Adjusted for 14.3% reduction in potential sales days.

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Past price hikes (e.g., 2026-09-28) led to sales drop from 16 to 10 units (37.5% drop). Adjusted for noise and limited data, apply conservative -10% effect.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 7.6 is adjusted for a store closure on Monday (1/7 of the week), reducing demand. The price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) is likely to reduce sales, especially since past price hikes (e.g., 2026-09-28) coincided with drops to 10 units. The planner note confirms a closure, a known demand reducer. No promotion or event is scheduled, and the classical model shows no uplift. The noise-adjusted effect of past price increases is modest, and the closure is a clear, single driver. No evidence of rebound or seasonal ramp beyond baseline. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited data on price impact.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 42.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 26.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
